content.text: {"utterance":"Now the invented case. One learner recites the proof flawlessly but cannot say why a step follows or handle a changed problem. Another explains haltingly, in different words, yet can adapt it. Iris, you doubted whether explanation is necessary; here the halting explainer seems to pass without fluency. But I ask the room: what exactly has the reciter learned? Is it nothing, or something, such as the sequence, that differs in kind from understanding? And what observation would decide between those answers?","cites":["SO1","SO2"],"memory":"Posed the proof-recitation versus halting-explanation case. Live question: does the reciter learn nothing or a different thing (sequence), and what observation decides? Watch whether students separate necessary from sufficient evidence."}
